[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Kubernetes Jobs, CronJobs, and Batch Processing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Batch processing is a common computing pattern for executing finite tasks, such as data processing, database backups, or running analytics. While Kubernetes is primarily designed for long-running services using Deployments and ReplicaSets, it provides native primitives like Jobs and CronJobs to handle finite, task-oriented workloads efficiently."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Kubernetes Jobs"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Job creates one or more Pods and ensures that a specified number of them successfully terminate. When the Job successfully completes, the Job object itself remains so you can view the completion status. Deleting a Job cleans up the Pods it created."},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here is an example of a basic Job manifest that calculates Pi to 2000 decimal places and prints the result:"},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: pi
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: pi
        image: perl:5.34
        command: ["perl", "-Mbignum=bpi", "-wle", "print bpi(2000)"]
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 4"},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Configuration Fields for Jobs"},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"restartPolicy: Unlike regular Pods, Jobs must have a restartPolicy of either OnFailure or Never. This ensures that the container does not restart infinitely upon completion or failure."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"backoffLimit: Specifies the number of retries before considering the Job failed. The default is 6. Kubernetes retries failed pods exponentially (10s, 20s, 40s... up to 6 minutes)."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"activeDeadlineSeconds: Limits the duration of a Job. If a Job takes longer than this threshold, all running pods are terminated and the Job is marked as failed."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Advanced Job Patterns"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Kubernetes supports three primary types of batch processing patterns using Jobs:"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Non-parallel Jobs: Typically, only one Pod is created unless the Pod fails. The Job is complete as soon as that Pod terminates successfully."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Parallel Jobs with a fixed completion count: You specify a 'completions' value. The Job launches multiple pods sequentially or concurrently until the successful completion count is reached."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Work Queue Jobs: You use a 'parallelism' value without specifying 'completions'. Multiple pods coordinate using a shared message queue (like RabbitMQ or Redis) to process items until the queue is empty."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Scheduling Tasks with CronJobs"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"CronJobs manage Jobs on a time-based schedule, mirroring the functionality of standard Unix cron utilities. Each CronJob creates a Job object roughly at each scheduled time."},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is an example of a CronJob that executes every minute:"},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: hello
spec:
  schedule: "* * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: hello
            image: busybox:1.28
            command:
            - /bin/sh
            - -c
            - date; echo Hello from the Kubernetes cluster
          restartPolicy: OnFailure"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"CronJob Concurrency Policies"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Because CronJobs create Jobs based on a schedule, overlapping runs can occur if a previous Job takes too long to finish. You can control this behavior using the concurrencyPolicy field:"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Allow (default): CronJobs allows concurrent Jobs to run simultaneously."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Forbid: If it is time for a new Job and the previous Job is still running, the CronJob skips the new run."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Replace: If it is time for a new Job and the previous Job is running, the current running Job is cancelled and replaced with the new Job."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"Kubernetes Jobs and CronJobs provide robust, native solutions for executing containerized batch workloads and scheduled maintenance tasks. By properly configuring backoff limits, restart policies, and concurrency handling, you can ensure reliable asynchronous processing within your cluster."}]
